claims.text: The starting material is a eutectic HEA consisting of an FCC matrix and ordered B2 precipitates.
The initial B2 phase has low or negligible local chemical order and behaves locally like a random solid solution.
The initial FCC/B2 phase boundaries are coherent.
Aging at approximately 650-1000 K induces substantial LCO in the B2 phase.
The proposed intermediate aging treatment does not produce grain coarsening or grain-boundary impurity segregation.
Increasing LCO in B2 raises complex stacking-fault energy.
Increasing LCO in B2 raises antiphase-boundary energy.
LCO creates a spatially heterogeneous, rugged energy landscape that acts as nanoscale obstacles to dislocations.
Dislocations in the LCO-rich B2 phase move through intermittent nanoscale segment detrapping rather than smooth propagation.
LCO-induced dislocation trapping increases the B2 critical resolved shear strength and slip activation barriers.
The increased barriers to B2 slip cause the dramatic intermediate-temperature loss of ductility.
Higher aging temperatures dissolve or substantially reduce LCO.
The B2 phase can undergo stress-induced martensitic transformation.
Stress-induced martensitic transformation makes the B2 phase more compliant, relieves stress concentrations, and restores ductility at higher aging temperatures.
Ductility should vary non-monotonically with aging temperature, progressing from ductile to brittle and then back to ductile.
The embrittlement regime lies where LCO is maximal, after LCO develops but before LCO dissolution or grain coarsening.
The embrittlement mechanism is confined to the B2 interior and immediate FCC/B2 interface rather than grain boundaries.
The exact embrittlement-temperature window depends on alloy-element diffusion coefficients.
Simulations indicate that a factor-of-three increase in shear stress is significant for the proposed transition in dislocation behavior.
B2 superlattice-peak intensity can quantify the proposed LCO evolution and discriminate it from a grain-boundary-controlled transition.

contradictions.description: The material is described as containing an ordered B2 phase while that same phase is described as having negligible chemical order and random-solid-solution-like behavior. A distinction between long-range B2 order and additional short-range LCO is needed to make these descriptions compatible.
